match.reason: None of the bank points teaches that a tangent to a circle meets the radius at 90° or that tangents from an outside point are equal; they all concern tangent lines to curves and gradients, which is a different idea.

rejected.title: Tangents to a circle
card: Tangent
A tangent is a line that touches a circle at exactly one point. That point is called the point of contact.
Radius rule
A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at \(90^{\circ}\). So the radius and the tangent form a right angle.
Equal tangents
Two tangents drawn from the same point outside a circle are equal in length. The length is measured from the outside point to each point of contact.
Example

A tangent meets a radius of a circle at A. The radius is 5 cm and the distance from the centre O to the outside point P is 13 cm. Triangle OAP has a right angle at A, so \(AP^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2} = 144\), and \(AP = 12\) cm.

2.alt: A circle with centre O. A radius runs from O to the point A on the circle. A tangent line touches the circle at A and is at right angles to the radius OA.

rejected.remember: A tangent is at right angles to the radius it touches. Tangents from one outside point are equal.

a.q: Which statement about a tangent and the radius to its point of contact is true?
opts: They are parallel to each other
a.why: A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at a right angle. Equal length applies to two tangents from the same outside point, not to a tangent and a radius.
a.clue: Think about the angle the card gives at the point of contact.

b.q: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from the point P to a circle with centre O, touching it at A and B. The radius is 6 cm and OP is 10 cm. What is the length of PB?
b.why: PB equals PA, and triangle OAP has a right angle at A. So \(PA^{2} = 10^{2} - 6^{2} = 64\), and PA and PB are 8 cm. Adding the squares gives \(\sqrt{136}\), which wrongly treats OP as a shorter side.
b.clue: Use the right angle at the point of contact, then equal tangents.

version.title: Tangents to a circle
card: Tangent
a line that touches a circle at exactly one point, called the point of contact. It does not cut into the circle.
Tangent and radius
the radius drawn to the point of contact meets the tangent at \(90^{\circ}\). This often makes a right-angled triangle with the centre.
Two tangents
from a point P outside a circle, two tangents can be drawn, touching it at A and B. They are equal in length, so \(PA = PB\).
Example: a circle has centre O and radius 5 cm, and \(OP = 13\) cm. Triangle OAP has its right angle at A, so \(PA^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2} = 144\). So \(PA = 12\) cm, and \(PB = 12\) cm too.
version.remember: The radius meets the tangent at \(90^{\circ}\). Two tangents from one outside point are equal in length.

a.q: PA is a tangent to a circle with centre O, touching it at A. Angle AOP is \(58^{\circ}\). What is angle APO?
a.why: The radius OA meets the tangent at \(90^{\circ}\), so triangle OAP has a right angle at A. Angle APO is \(180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 58^{\circ} = 32^{\circ}\). The answer \(122^{\circ}\) leaves out the right angle at A.
a.clue: Find the right angle in triangle OAP first.

b.q: Tangents from the point P touch a circle with centre O at A and B. The radius is 8 cm and \(OP = 17\) cm. What is \(PA + PB\)?
b.why: Triangle OAP has a right angle at A, so \(PA^{2} = 17^{2} - 8^{2} = 225\) and \(PA = 15\) cm. Tangents from P are equal, so \(PB = 15\) cm and the total is 30 cm. The answer 15 cm stops after finding only PA.
b.clue: Use the right angle at A, then the equal tangents.

wants.brief: A circle with centre O and a point P outside it. Two tangents from P touch the circle at A and B. The radii OA and OB are drawn, each with a small right-angle mark where it meets its tangent. The interval OP is drawn. PA and PB each have one small equal-length tick. Label only O, A, B and P.
wants.why: Seeing both tangents, the two right angles and the triangles OAP and OBP shows where each rule applies.
